supported: The observed raw hierarchy is much larger than expected from independent Poisson counting error or the frozen Gamma-Poisson CV10% sensitivity.
The raw hierarchy is not unusual under the frozen Gamma-Poisson CV20% sensitivity.
The stronger detrended and annual-growth hierarchy cannot be used as measurement-error-robust evidence because the error-only null commonly generates effects of the observed scale.
Annual growth ordering in which all three within-island beta values exceed among-island beta is expected almost always under the error-only null.
not_supported: a claim that the hierarchical buffering result is robust to the full frozen count-error family
promotion of detrended or annual-growth beta as stronger confirmatory evidence
a claim that CV20% represents empirically calibrated Palmer observer error
a claim that counting error caused the observed hierarchy
ecological_interpretation: The raw subcolony-to-island variability reduction exceeds what low-to-moderate independent count error generates, but the present census lacks record-level observer-error metadata needed to distinguish that biological signal from a conservative 20% multiplicative-error scenario. The hierarchy should therefore be treated as measurement-error-sensitive descriptive evidence, while the N_eff coefficient remains separately robust under its frozen count-error diagnostic.
